title: Form states: focus-within, valid, invalid
summary: :focus-within lights up the active row; :user-invalid and :placeholder-shown react to what was typed.
explanation: :focus-within matches an element when it or anything inside it has focus. The whole row, label included, highlights while you type in its input, which :focus alone cannot do because a label never gets focus.

An email input knows when its text is not an email. :user-invalid matches only after the person has typed and left the field, so the form does not shout at them before they start (:invalid would be red immediately).
:placeholder-shown is true while the field is empty, so the hint under the input hides as soon as there is text.
tryThis: Click into each field and press Tab between them.
Type abc into the email field and press Tab: it turns red. Then type a real address.
Change :user-invalid to :invalid: the empty email field is not red, but abc is red while you are still typing.
